title.narrative: Output 7.5. Increased capacity of Member States to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: 1. Training materials and handbooks on new legislative frameworks including employment in fishing vessels were developed by MOLISA to disseminate information on the new law protecting labour rights of migrant workers, including migrant fishers in 2023. 2. Eight (8) MRCs in eight (8) provinces provided 6,328 migrant workers, including migrant workers, with information, counseling and services; three (3) of these MRCs were established in 2022 in Lao Cai, Thai Binh, and Nghe An. 3. An e-commerce training manual developed and introduced by the National Institute for Vocational Education and Training (NIVET) among 210 women migrant workers who had been seriously affected by the COVID-19 pandemic and needed to develop new livelihood skills. The e-commerce manual helped women migrant workers to be better aware of how to minimize risks to violence in cyberspace which has become an emerging concern in Viet Nam. 1. With the support of the European Union (EU), ILO supported the development of training materials and handbooks on the new legislative framework including employment in fishing vessels in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City. 2. With the support of the EU, ILO partnered with DOLAB to establish three new MRCs, and with the support of the Australian and Canadian governments, and the EU, built the capacity of the MRC personnel to provide information and services to migrant workers. 3. ILO collaborated with NIVET to enhance the employability skills of women migrant workers while developing the E-commerce training manual based on a consolidation of international best practices. ILO’s contribution was made with the support of the EU.
